fact_check_verdict: PASS WITH CUTS. Two adversarial validators. UAF Geophysical Institute release (Rod Boyce, September 16th/17th) read in full, Fairbanks Daily News-Miner November 19th (Jack Barnwell, Cahill's chamber talk) read, KTUU September 23rd/24th and DroneLife September 22nd corroborate. Alaska DOH Year 2 release November 17th read (PDF rendered). CMS August 25th, ADN August 17th, Alaska DOT&PF and Tanana Chiefs Conference pages read. 1925 serum run from the Alaska State Archives and the UAF Alaska Science Forum. Conditions: the flight was PILOTED by ACUASI pilots, never autonomous; the 1,000 km was a LOOP out of and back to Nenana, never a delivery; no lab results were published, so 'the blood survived' is Cahill's statement; the samples were not tested for doping or medical conditions; detect-and-avoid radar is PLANNED; the TCC and Ryan Air grants' purpose is not stated by the News-Miner, only that both partner with ACUASI on medical delivery operations; ADN alone reports $250,000 for TCC drones; CMS's quarter-million framework names no recipient; no Ryan Air amount; FAA rule status in November 2026 unverified, so say only that FAA rules regulate against flying beyond the operator's sight; $1.3 billion is the five-year program per the News-Miner, not money received.

claims.spoken: On August 19th a drone took off from Nenana Municipal Airport and landed back there.
claims.verbatim_source: "The test began and ended at Nenana Municipal Airport on Aug. 19."
requires: round trip, never a destination
date is background, the in-window peg is November 19th

claims.spoken: It flew 1,000 kilometers in a loop.
claims.verbatim_source: "successfully completed a 1,000-kilometer test flight carrying human blood samples"
requires: a loop that started and ended in Nenana (KTUU: in a circle in the sky at between 3,000 and 5,000 feet), never point to point

claims.spoken: The flight lasted 8 hours and 47 minutes.
claims.verbatim_source: "The 8-hour, 47-minute flight by the Alaska Center for Unmanned Aircraft Systems Integration"

claims.spoken: It carried human blood samples.
claims.verbatim_source: "successfully completed a 1,000-kilometer test flight carrying human blood samples"
requires: samples or sample tubes, never vials, never an amount in pounds

claims.spoken: The test was for the International Testing Agency, which runs anti-doping checks in sport.
claims.verbatim_source: "Labelled non-quotation: both pages describe the test as conducted for the International Testing Agency, the anti-doping body"

claims.spoken: The samples weren't tested for doping or for medical conditions.
claims.verbatim_source: "The samples contained no personally identifying information and were not evaluated for doping or medical conditions."

claims.spoken: Each volunteer gave two samples, so blood that flew could be compared with blood that stayed on the ground.
claims.on_screen: TWO SAMPLES EACH · ONE FLEW · ONE STAYED
claims.verbatim_source: "Each volunteer provided two samples for comparison of conditions before and after transport."
requires: the ground comparison wording comes from KTUU (tested against samples that had been kept on the ground)
draw tubes, never vials in the copy

claims.spoken: The aircraft is a Windracers ULTRA, a twin-engine cargo drone.
claims.verbatim_source: "ACUASI owns two of the twin-engine aircraft, which have a 31-foot wingspan"

claims.spoken: It has a 31-foot wingspan.
claims.verbatim_source: "which have a 31-foot wingspan"

claims.spoken: It can carry 200 pounds of cargo.
claims.verbatim_source: "a range of about 600 miles, a 200-pound cargo capacity and three cargo drop doors."

claims.spoken: Its range is about 600 miles.
claims.verbatim_source: "a range of about 600 miles, a 200-pound cargo capacity and three cargo drop doors."

claims.spoken: UAF's drone center owns two of them.
claims.verbatim_source: "ACUASI owns two of the twin-engine aircraft, which have a 31-foot wingspan"

claims.spoken: Pilots at UAF's drone center flew it remotely.
claims.verbatim_source: "The competency of ACUASI pilots is truly outstanding,"

remotely from KTUU (aircraft being piloted remotely)

claims.spoken: Cathy Cahill directs UAF's drone center.

claims.verbatim_source: "Labelled non-quotation: the News-Miner headline and body identify Cahill as ACUASI director"

claims.verbatim_source: "What this proves is that the blood could survive a long-distance flight at elevation and not get degraded."
